title: The Magician, top half
prompt: The top half of a tarot card depicting The Magician that has been ripped in half. I’d like the art style of the card to be like a child’s coloring book, so it should still accurately depict the archetypes and motifs and so forth traditionally used on The Magician tarot cards, but in the line art style of a coloring book that you might find in a third grade classroom

responses.notes: Generated via clean-context subagent; standard technical appendix v1 appended to the prompt. Refined: the one-shot left the card face transparent — a literal reading of the appendix's "transparent background (no opaque backdrop rectangle)" — and the owner's second prompt asked for a parchment colored background on the card. The revision adds one closed path tracing the card outline and continuing down through the torn edge, filled #f3e3c1 with no stroke, beneath all the linework, so the paper stops exactly at the rip rather than behind it; the canvas outside the card stays transparent. Nothing else in the drawing changed between the two turns. Ink-bounds check passed — worst dead margin 1.5%; no viewBox normalization. Iterated internally during the first turn (rendered its own pass, then reworked arms, hair, snake belt and the rip's irregularity) before answering — still a single response. Motif coverage is the widest of the three: lemniscate over the head, double-ended wand held in a drawn fist, ouroboros belt with a head biting its own tail and diamond scale marks, rose arbour overhead with vines down both margins, garden lilies, and the Roman numeral I as an outlined serif glyph. The rip is a 33-vertex zigzag that doubles as the parchment fill's lower boundary, so tear and paper share one edge. Unlike the other two it uses no clipPath — every stroke is hand-terminated near the tear instead of being cut by the card shape, which is where the strained integrity shows: the arms are open stroke pairs rather than closed limb outlines, and robe and vine lines run to hand-tuned stops around the rip. Every <use> carries both xlink:href and href.

Card outline is stroked twice — once under the clipped linework and once over it — so the border stays crisp against the tear. Limbs are flat quadrilaterals meeting the robe at visible seams, and the scattered eight-pointed stars are an addition the prompt didn't call for, though a small one within the tarot idiom.
